newsitem.title: CANADA: Rigel sees '97 financial, production gains.
newsitem.headline: Rigel sees '97 financial, production gains.

text.p: Rigel Energy Corp, buoyed recently by speculation over what appears to be a huge oil discovery in the North Sea, expects higher cash flow and earnings this year, Rigel Chief Executive Don West said on Wednesday.
West said Rigel's cash flow for 1997 was expected to climb to C$147 million or C$2.62 a share, up from C$134.7 million or C$2.40 a share last year.
Earnings were projected at C$8 million or C$0.14 a share, up from C$2.4 million or C$0.04 a share in 1996.

The company's production was expected to average 18,500 barrels of oil and 180 million cubic feet of natural gas this year, up slightly from 18,250 barrels of oil and 156.2 million cubic feet a day of gas last year.

The small average output gains would be a result of the company's sale last year of 30 percent of its western Canadian oil and gas properties, representing about keight percent of its production, West said at Rigel's annual meeting.
The company budgeted capital spending this year of C$158 million and expected to drill 180 wells, compared to spending of C$125 million and 188 wells last year.
Rigel drew a standing-room-only crowd of analysts, bankers and investors anxious to hear details of the Moray Firth oil discovery at UK Block 13/24b off the east coast of Scotland.
Excitement over the play has lifted the company's stock by over C$3 since the beginning of the month, a move that may have taken Rigel off the list of potential takeover targets.

Production tests at a discovery well drilled this spring by BG Plc, formerly British Gas, yielded 2,600 barrels of oil a day. West said the well could have pump four or five times more than that if not for mechanical problems during testing.
Several aspects of the discovery, whose partners include BG Exploration with 50 percent, Amerada Hess Corp with 30 percent and Rigel with 20 percent, remain confidential.

But West told the meeting that reports of 600 million barrels of oil in place were likely conservative and that the field could harbor as much as 900 million barrels with a recovery factor of 30 percent to 40 percent.
The companies planned to drill an appraisal well in the region before the end of the year and full development could start producing by late 1999 or early 2000, West said.
Development costs for the play -- which has the potential to double Rigel's reserves -- would be about US$1.0 billion with the use of waterflood recovery technology, he said.
"Our partners are every bit as excited as us to get on with this thing," he said. "There will be no holding back."
He declined to disclose the size of the pay zone and which geological zone was tapped by the discovery well.

West said the company's reserves, boosted also by the possibilities of big discoveries of gas in the foothills of southwestern Alberta and onshore northern Ireland and oil at Moose Mountain, Alberta, could grow to 385 million barrels of oil equivalent by 2000, on a proved plus half probable basis.
Reserves at the end of 1996 were 126 million barrels.
Rigel shares were trading up 0.85 on Monday to 16.50. The stock has climbed from 13.45 on May 2. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
